statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). Six hours after the Globex reopen the 28,981.00-29,100.00 band is still exactly unchanged, but NQ has eased back to mid-band at 29,028.50 (-1.22%) from -1.10% an hour ago and WTI has returned to 103.04, near its 103.58 session high. Those two reversals undo the reasons Tail was cut a point, so Tail maps back to 20 while Stress stays high at 77 on a 10-year near 4.98%, unresolved Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb supply risk and a Wednesday FOMC with projections.
recommendation: Tail sits at the bottom of the watch band and well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 13:00-16:00 UTC, covering the 13:30 UTC US cash open and the first full cash hour, which is the first US auction to price the weekend AI-pacing story and the Middle East escalation; the conditional forecast peaks at 24 there and stays below the block band. The named invalidation for the constructive structural read is unchanged: a decisive loss of the 28,981.00 reopen low on shallow pullbacks, with the 07:00 UTC European cash open the next test. Monday's US calendar holds only routine 3-month and 6-month bill auctions at 15:30 UTC.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold an unchanged 28,981-29,100 band for a sixth hour at -1.22% while Hormuz talks are postponed and WTI returns to 103
body: A sixth consecutive hour of live price-path evidence leaves the structural read constructive but slightly less so than an hour ago. NQ is quoted at 29,028.50, down 358.50 or 1.22% against the 29,387.00 reference close, as of 23:16 EDT, and a second independent quote on a later contract month shows the same -1.21%, so the level is well corroborated. The decisive structural fact is unchanged: the front-month day range is still exactly 28,981.00 to 29,100.00, the same 119-point band printed in the first hour after the reopen. Six hours without range expansion, and without a chain of failed retracements, is the opposite of the price path that overwhelms a mean-reversion book. Two details nonetheless argue against cutting Tail further. Price has rotated back out of the upper half of the band to mid-band, giving back the improvement that justified last hour's one-point cut, and WTI has climbed back to 103.04, up 2.99%, near its 103.58 session high after briefly backing off it. Both of the specific reasons for that cut have therefore reversed inside one hour, so Tail returns to 20 at the bottom of the watch band. The wider Asian tape supports the constructive structural reading rather than undercutting it. The Nikkei is 63,498.61, down 0.80%, after trading as low as 62,726.18, roughly -2.0%, so Japan has retraced well over half of its initial drop. The KOSPI is 6,760.69, down 2.16%, after a 6,654.82 low near -3.7%. Korea remains the pressure point given the index weight of Samsung and SK hynix and crowded AI positioning, but both markets have produced genuine, completed retracements rather than one-way slides. That is working mean reversion in the cash markets most directly exposed to the weekend story. Stress rises a point to 77 and stays in the high band. The rates backdrop is marginally worse, with the 10-year at 4.98%, the 2-year at 4.64% and the 30-year at 5.37%, the long end near its highest since October 2023. The energy and geopolitical picture is the more material change in this hour's evidence: the Hormuz shipping-lane meeting between Iran and Gulf nations has been postponed indefinitely, an Iranian commercial vessel was struck near Qeshm Island, and Houthi pressure around Bab el-Mandeb raises the prospect of two major energy chokepoints being disrupted at once. That is an unresolved, headline-driven escalation, and it is the main reason the conditional forecast does not decay faster. The counterweight is that cash volatility entered this episode low, with the VIX closing Friday at 15.84 after an 11% decline, so the futures-implied move higher is off a subdued base. Dominant mode stays mixed: an equity market repricing lower on an AI-pacing narrative, crude and yields firm, and contained two-way rotation in the index itself. Shared cross-asset context from the repository collector was not used as live evidence this run, since it was collected at 01:45 UTC and carries a partial collection status; the assessment rests on the primary sources listed.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available. Tail rose steadily through the weekend from 6 at 03:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC, eased to 16, then stepped through 17, 18, 18, 19, 21 and 22 as the Globex reopen approached and arrived, crossing into the watch band at 21:00 UTC, before settling back to 20 for three hours and to 19 in the final hour as the reopen low held. The mapped state was EA_ON and green for the first 18 hours, WATCH and yellow for five hours across the reopen, and EA_ON again in the final hour. Stress climbed without interruption from 59 to 78 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, then eased to 77 and 76. Confidence held near 86 through the weekend, stepped down to the low-to-mid 70s from 16:00 UTC as the evidence gap widened, then recovered through 78, 80, 82, 84 and 85 once the reopen restored a live price path. Dominant mode was normal for 19 of the 24 hours, event/whipsaw across the reopen hour itself, and mixed for the final four.
outlookSummary: The concentrated conditional risk stays in the 13:00-16:00 UTC stretch around the 13:30 UTC US cash open, the first US auction to price both the weekend AI-pacing story and the Hormuz escalation, and the forecast peaks at 24 in the first full cash hour, one point below the block band, rather than entering it on structure that has not been observed. Two nearer checkpoints precede it: the Japanese cash close near 06:00 UTC, and more importantly the 07:00 UTC European cash open, where conditional Tail rises to 22 as the first deep non-Asian pool to price the story. Between them the base case is continued absorption, with Tail decaying to 19 through the European pre-US lull. The standing caveat is that the Middle East supply situation is unresolved and headline-driven, so a discontinuity would not respect a quiet-hour base case. The named invalidation throughout is a decisive break of the 28,981.00 reopen low accompanied by shallow or failed pullbacks; every hour beyond the current one is scored conditionally and no later price structure is treated as already observed.
